about: Details of every /api/* route in routes.json, used by openapi.py to build docs/api/openapi.json. Routes, methods and auth come from routes.json; response documents reference the contract schemas in specs/001-platform-bootstrap/contracts/schemas by file name. 'action' means the shared action-result schema.

tags.name: Roof
tags.description: Move the roof and clear a fault.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: Read and change the device's settings.

tags.name: Alerts
tags.description: Alerts: whether they're sent, recent ones, tests.

GET /api/status.description: Firmware, memory, flash, time, WiFi (with IPv6 addresses), MQTT, alerts, Alpaca clients and connections. Also pushed over `/ws/status`.

GET /api/settings/effective.description: Each setting that depends on another, and whether it's in effect or inactive, with the reason.

GET /api/config.description: Every setting. Passwords and keys are masked. The `X-Config-Revision` response header carries the settings revision, read before the settings (spec 021): it changes on every save, starts from a random value at each start, and a save can send it back as `baseRevision`.

POST /api/config.description: Partial update: only the fields sent change. A masked or empty password keeps the stored one; `null` clears it. Spec 021: a page sends `baseRevision` (the revision it loaded) and `baseValues` (the values it loaded for the fields it changes). At the current revision the save goes through; at another one, only if each base value still matches the device's (secrets compare masked); otherwise 409 with `conflicts` (the dotted names, at most 16) and `revision`, and nothing is saved. Without `baseRevision` nothing is checked. The answer carries the new `revision`. A wrong value is refused with `error` naming it; a setting whose dependency is off is saved and reported inactive by `/api/settings/effective`. Refused with 409 while the roof is opening or closing or a close is waiting to start (flash writes stall its control task); while the save runs, an open is refused and a close waits for it.

POST /api/sqmeter/site.description: Spec 020: the device fetches the SQMeter's `GET /api/config` (SQMeter sends no CORS headers, so a browser can't) and answers with what the setup wizard and Settings can copy: its location, time zone and NTP servers, MQTT broker, port, user name and base topic, and ntfy server and topic. Each secret (MQTT password, ntfy token, Pushover user key and app token) is only ever reported as set or not: its value never appears, even from an SQMeter that doesn't mask it. Parts an older SQMeter lacks are `null`. Nothing is saved. The address is the body's `url`, else `safety.http.url`, in any form the address setting takes (`192.168.1.50`, `sqmeter.local`, `https://sqmeter.lan`, or a URL ending in one of SQMeter's API paths); only its scheme, host and port are used. https is encrypted without a certificate check. The login sent to SQMeter (HTTP Basic) is the body's `username` and `password` when given (the password mask means the saved one), else the saved `safety.http` login, which only goes to the saved SQMeter's host and port. Refused (409) while the roof moves, a close waits or the automatic close works, and while another copy runs; 502 when SQMeter doesn't answer, wants a password ("SQMeter wants a password"), refuses the one sent ("SQMeter refused the password"), or the reply isn't SQMeter's settings.

url.description: SQMeter's address as typed (e.g. 192.168.1.50, sqmeter.local or https://sqmeter.lan). Optional: the saved address when left out.

username.description: SQMeter's user name (HTTP Basic), as typed. Optional: the saved one when left out and the address is the saved SQMeter's host and port.

password.description: SQMeter's password, as typed; the mask (********) or leaving it out means the saved one, which only goes to the saved SQMeter's host and port. Never logged or echoed.

address.description: The SQMeter's scheme, host and port, e.g. http://192.168.1.50.

POST /api/sqmeter/test.description: Spec 020: the device reads SQMeter's `GET /api/safety` once, as the weather poll does, at the body's address and login (as `POST /api/sqmeter/site` takes them), and answers with SQMeter's verdict. Nothing is saved and the weather source is unchanged. 200 with `safe`, `reasonFlags` and a `text` for people; 502 with `error` when SQMeter doesn't answer ("SQMeter not answering: ..."), wants or refuses a password, or the address answers but not like SQMeter's /api/safety ("That address answered HTTP 404, not like SQMeter's /api/safety", "That address answered, but not like SQMeter's /api/safety (missing safe)"). Refused (409) while the roof moves, a close waits or the automatic close works, and while another read of SQMeter runs.

url.description: SQMeter's address as typed (e.g. 192.168.1.50, sqmeter.local or https://sqmeter.lan). Optional: the saved address when left out.

username.description: SQMeter's user name (HTTP Basic), as typed. Optional: the saved one when left out and the address is the saved SQMeter's host and port.

password.description: SQMeter's password, as typed; the mask (********) or leaving it out means the saved one, which only goes to the saved SQMeter's host and port. Never logged or echoed.

safe.description: SQMeter's verdict (false whenever it sets a reason flag).

text.description: For people: "SQMeter says safe" or "SQMeter says unsafe: reasonFlags 0x200 (rain)".

PUT /api/config.description: The same as `POST /api/config`, for clients that use PUT, including the `baseRevision` check (spec 021). Refused with 409 while the roof is opening or closing or a close is waiting to start (flash writes stall its control task); while the save runs, an open is refused and a close waits for it.

POST /api/backup.description: The backup file: every setting as `GET /api/config` shows it, with a header. With a `passphrase` (8 characters or more) the passwords, keys and tokens are included encrypted (AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256); without one the file holds no secret. Answered from a background task: a second or two with a passphrase. Refusals carry a `code`: 400 `passphrase-short`, 409 `busy` while another backup or preview runs, 413 `too-large`.

POST /api/backup/preview.description: Reads a backup file (`backup`, its text or its JSON) and, with its `passphrase`, its secrets, and answers what applying would save: the settings (masked), which secrets change, settings this board can't use and why it would restart. Nothing is applied; the `token` binds this preview to `POST /api/backup/apply`. Refused with `code` `not-backup`, `damaged`, `newer-format`, `wrong-passphrase` or `invalid` (the save's own reason in `error`).

backup.description: The backup file's text, or its JSON.

POST /api/backup/apply.description: Saves exactly the settings the preview with this `token` showed, as one settings save, and restarts the device about 2 s later when `restarting` is true. 409 `stale` when the preview was already applied or replaced, is older than 10 minutes, or the settings changed since: preview again. Refused with 409 while the roof is opening or closing or a close is waiting to start (flash writes stall its control task), and, when it would restart, also while the automatic close is waiting for the park or closing.

POST /api/restart.description: Restarts the device after answering. Refused with 409 (with the reason) while the roof is opening or closing, a close is waiting to start, or the automatic close is waiting for the park or closing.

POST /api/roof/open.description: Asks the roof to open, as a person. Refused unless the weather verdict is safe (constitution III), and by the motion logic (a latched fault, the Hall reading not settled, the supply low or unreadable, current sense on and unreadable, invalid settings), and with `busy` while an upload or command-line OTA is writing the flash, an MQTT connect is under way or a restart is scheduled. An accepted open starts after the 500 ms dead time and ends on the open magnet; `GET /api/status` `roof` shows its progress. An open in progress stops if the weather stops being safe. Refused with `hotspot` while the setup hotspot, which has no password, is on. Needs the header `X-RoofRoof: 1`.

state.description: The roof's state after the command.

reason.description: Why it was refused (409 only): `weatherNotSafe`, `daylight` (open only: the daylight setting is "alert and close" and the sun is up, spec 013), `mountNotParked`, `faultLatched`, `hallNotSettled`, `positionUnknown`, `supplyLow`, `supplyUnreadable`, `currentUnreadable`, `settingsInvalid`, `busy` (an upload or other flash write, a WiFi change or scan, an MQTT connect or a scheduled restart; open only), `restarting` (a restart about to happen), `hotspot` (open while the setup hotspot is on) or `notStarted`.

error.description: The refusal for people, with the measured value and the limit or the input that failed (409 only).

pending.description: A close accepted that starts once an upload or MQTT connect has stopped (202 only).

message.description: What the waiting close is waiting for (202 only).

POST /api/roof/close.description: Asks the roof to close, as a person. Refused unless the mount is confirmed parked: N.I.N.A. reports it at park and every fitted park switch reads closed (constitution II); refused by the motion logic as for open. A close in progress stops with a `parkInterlock` fault if the park confirmation is lost. Needs the header `X-RoofRoof: 1`. A close always wins: it cancels a scheduled restart and stops an upload in progress (the upload fails with 409). While an upload, another flash write or an MQTT connect is still finishing, the close is accepted with 202 and `pending: true` and starts as soon as it is done (`roof.closePending` in the status).

POST /api/roof/calibration/start.description: Spec 016: an attended run, started only by a person at the roof. From where the roof is, a slow close to the closed end (unless `at` is `closed`), a slow open and a slow close, and with `topPass` an open and a close at the top duty; each leg stops at the first magnet and is bounded by `roof.calibrationLimitSeconds` (later legs by the measured ones), the existing faults and the drive budget. Refused (409, with `reason` and `error`) unless `attended` is true, the weather is safe, daylight doesn't want the roof closed, the mount is confirmed parked, the automatic close is idle, no fault is latched, the roof is at rest, nothing blocks an open and the Hall reading agrees with `at`. Reasons: `notAttended`, `calibrating`, `closeSequence`, `faultLatched`, `moving`, `closeWaiting`, `settingsPending`, `weatherNotSafe`, `daylight`, `mountNotParked`, `busy`, `hotspot`, `restarting`, `invalid`, `hallDisagrees`, `notStarted`, or the motion logic's (`supplyLow`, `supplyUnreadable`, `currentUnreadable`, `hallNotSettled`, `settingsInvalid`). Read the run with `GET /api/roof/calibration`. Nothing is saved: the proposal is accepted with `POST /api/config`. Needs the header `X-RoofRoof: 1`.

attended.description: The person confirms they are at the roof and can see it; must be true.

travelMm.description: The travel between the magnets' trigger points, measured with a tape.

topPass.description: Also open and close at the top duty (default false).

state.description: `running` when accepted; the roof's state when refused.

reason.description: Why it was refused (409 only); see the operation's description.

atOpenEnd.description: The roof is now fully open.

GET /api/roof/calibration.description: Spec 016: the last calibration run since start-up (`idle` before any): its state, the leg under way with its limit, how it ended, each measured leg (time, duty, end level, speed at 100 % duty, current and supply), the Hall readings (in between, and at rest at each end) and, for a finished run, the proposal with the value at the start beside each proposed one (`null` where withheld, with the reason). Read-only, kept in memory only.

GET /api/roof/inputs.description: The weather verdict with each SQMeter source's state and reason, the park result, and N.I.N.A.'s last mount reading (connected, at park, slewing), as the device last polled them. Read-only: it sends nothing to SQMeter or N.I.N.A. The setup wizard's Tests read it.

GET /api/wifi/scan.description: The first call starts a background scan and answers 202 with `scanning: true`; call again about once a second until `scanning` is false and the list arrives. Refused with 409 while the roof is opening or closing, a close is waiting to start or the automatic close is waiting for the park or closing (the radio leaves its channel during a scan); while a scan runs (at most 15 s), an open is refused and a close waits.

POST /api/wifi/connect.description: What the WiFi setup screen uses. Answers 202 at once; poll `/api/status` (`wifi.connectPending`, then `wifi.connected`). On success the network is saved and the device restarts onto it 15 s later. Send `""` as the password for an open network. Refused with 409 (with the reason) while the roof is opening or closing, a close is waiting to start, or the automatic close is waiting for the park or closing: it drops the current network for up to 10 s. Until it has joined (at most 15 s), an open is refused and a close waits.

POST /api/mqtt/test.description: Tries to connect with the given details without saving them. A `password` of `********` (the mask settings return) or empty means the saved password, which is only used when broker, port and username match the saved ones; for any other broker a masked password is refused with 400.

POST /api/update.description: A firmware `.bin` for this device's build and partition layout. 400 when the file is for another layout (nothing changed); 500 keeps the running firmware. The device restarts on success. Refused with 409 (with the reason) before anything is written while the roof is opening or closing, a close is waiting to start, or the automatic close is waiting for the park or closing (a new firmware may not read what it keeps across a restart); the restart after it waits for the roof and the close. An upload in progress is stopped by a roof close (409, "Upload stopped: the roof is closing").

POST /api/update/fs.description: A LittleFS image that fills the web UI partition exactly. A file for another layout is refused before anything is erased. Settings are kept. Refused with 409 (with the reason) while the roof is opening or closing, a close is waiting to start, or the automatic close is waiting for the park or closing (flash writes stall the control task, and the restart after it can't be cancelled). An upload in progress is stopped by a roof close (409, "Upload stopped: the roof is closing").

GET /api/alerts/armed.description: Whether alerts are being sent, the send mode and why it's sending or paused.

POST /api/alerts/arm.description: Takes effect at once and survives restarts.

POST /api/alerts/disarm.description: While paused nothing is sent. Takes effect at once and survives restarts.

GET /api/alerts/recent.description: Whether alerts are on, and the last 20 since boot, newest first, with each channel's delivery result (`pending`, `sent`, `failed`, `skipped`).

POST /api/alerts/test.description: Queues a test on the given saved, switched-on channel(s); see `/api/alerts/recent` for the result. A channel that can't deliver right now is recorded as `skipped`. Add `event`, `level` and `sound` for a sample of that event, or `title`/`message` to try custom wording with `{variables}`.

GET /api/diag.description: Everything the controller measures now: the supply and its sag, the motor current and power, the duty, direction and ramp phase, the driver's EN and PWM levels, the Hall reading, the position estimate with the elapsed and remaining time and the timeout, the drive budget, the control task's step time and gap, the watchdog margin, the main loop's pass time, memory, stacks, Wi-Fi signal, uptime and reset reason. The same document streams on /ws/diag. With advanced diagnostics off it is {"enabled": false}.

GET /api/diag/moves.description: The last 32 move summaries, newest first, each saying whether its profile is still held (the last 5 moves). The same handler serves /api/diag/moves/{id}: one move with its summary and downsampled profile (404 when it isn't held), or with ?format=csv the profile as a CSV download. With advanced diagnostics off the list is {"enabled": false}.

POST /api/diag/moves/clear.description: Empties the move log and the summary list, and the kept summaries at the next flash write the device allows. Needs the X-RoofRoof: 1 header. Refused while the roof moves or a close waits, so the move in progress isn't lost.

POST /api/roof/jog.description: Spec 019: a person at the roof moves it at the slow duty while they hold a button. Without `id` it starts a jog toward `direction`; with the `id` it answered, it renews that jog. The device stops the jog by itself `holdMs` (500 ms) after the last renewal reached it, by its own control steps, at the first magnet after leaving the one it started on, and after 30 s (or a move from an unknown position's timeout, if shorter) with the `timeout` fault; every motion fault and the drive budget apply. Release with the `id` and `release: true`, which stops that jog only (a person's `POST /api/roof/stop` stops it too). Both directions need the weather safe, daylight not wanting the roof closed and the mount confirmed parked (the motor direction setting may still be wrong), and the park interlock watches every jog. Start refusals (409): `notAttended`, `calibrating`, `closeSequence`, `faultLatched`, `moving`, `closeWaiting`, `settingsPending`, `weatherNotSafe`, `daylight`, `mountNotParked`, `busy`, `hotspot`, `restarting`, `notStarted`, or the motion logic's (`supplyLow`, `supplyUnreadable`, `currentUnreadable`, `hallNotSettled`, `settingsInvalid`). A renewal or release of a jog that has ended is refused with `jogEnded` and never starts one. While a jog runs, open and close are refused with `jogging`. Needs the header `X-RoofRoof: 1`.

direction.description: Toward the open or the closed end (through `roof.openDirection`). Needed to start or renew a jog.

attended.description: The person confirms they are at the roof and can see it; must be true to start a jog.

id.description: Renew this jog instead of starting one.

release.description: With `id` alone: the button was let go; stop that jog.

state.description: The roof's state after the request.

id.description: The jog running, to renew it with (200 only).

holdMs.description: The device stops the jog when it hasn't been renewed for this long (200 only).

keepAliveMs.description: How often to renew it while the button is held (200 only).

limitMs.description: The jog's hard timeout (200 only); the page releases a second before it.

reason.description: Why it was refused (409 only); see the operation's description.

error.description: The refusal for people, with the measured value and the limit or the input that failed (409 only).

POST /api/roof/teach/mark.description: Spec 019: records the Hall reading over the last second at rest (count, mean, lowest, highest, noise) as the closed end, the open end or a place part-way. Refused (409) with `notAtRest` while the roof moves or a jog runs or before it has been still for a second, `hallNotSettled` while the reading is unsettled or at a rail, and `calibrating` during a calibration run. Needs the header `X-RoofRoof: 1`.

POST /api/roof/teach/confirm.description: Spec 019: saves the proposal of `GET /api/roof/teach` (`roof.hallHighEnd`, `roof.hallHighCounts`, `roof.hallLowCounts`) over the current settings through the settings save, when the values sent are the proposal (409 `proposalChanged`, or `noProposal`). Refused like every settings save while the roof moves or a platform action holds it (409), and 400 if the result isn't valid. Then the marks are cleared, and once the settings are applied the roof's position follows the magnet it sits on. Needs the header `X-RoofRoof: 1`.

POST /api/roof/teach/discard.description: Spec 019: drops the marks and the proposal; changes no setting. Always accepted. Needs the header `X-RoofRoof: 1`.

GET /api/roof/teach.description: Spec 019: the jog under way (its id, direction, time driven, limit, keep-alive deadline and interval), whether the roof has been still for the one-second reading window and its mean, the three marks, and the proposal (`null` until all three are marked; `ok` false with the reason when the ends can't be told apart or the part-way reading overlaps one). Read-only, kept in memory only.

GET /api/pins.description: Spec 023: the pins in effect since the last start (`running`) and as saved, whether a restart is needed to apply the saved ones, whether the pins in effect passed the pin rules at boot (with the reason and every error and warning), whether the chip has PSRAM, the board in effect and, with no board chosen, the board the boot probe found (`detected`; `null` when it didn't run), the presets, and each board's Ethernet and header pins. Read-only.

POST /api/pins/validate.description: Spec 023: the pin rules' errors and warnings for a pin map on this chip, without saving it. A named preset alone fills in its pins; pins sent with a named preset that differ from it are an error. Save a map through `POST /api/config` (`pins`).

issues.text: RPWM on GPIO35: GPIO35 is input only and can't drive an output

POST /api/pins/check.description: Spec 023: starts the wiring check on the device's main loop; read the result with `GET /api/pins/check`. Nothing can move the roof: EN is read for about 50 µs as an input with the internal pull-up while both PWM stay low. Refused (409) while the roof moves, a close waits, the close sequence works, a calibration run or a jog is under way, while the pins in effect are invalid or no board is chosen, while a pin change waits for a restart, and while a check runs.

GET /api/pins/check.description: Spec 023: the last wiring check since start-up (`idle` before any): each check's level, reading and text, and `suggestPreset` when the Ethernet probe found a WT32-ETH01 on a board set up without Ethernet. Direction and travel aren't checked (the `motion` item points to the calibration page's jog and teach).

checks.text: EN reads low with the internal pull-up: its pull-down holds the driver off
Direction and travel need the roof to move: use Jog and teach the ends on the calibration page
